guidance.heading: Financial outlook and guidance: visible growth and resilience
section: – Financial outlook over the five-year period from 2026/27 to 2030/31:
– total cumulative capital investment of at least £70 billion;
– Group asset growth CAGR1 of around 10%;
– driving underlying EPS CAGR2 of 8–10% from the 2025/26 EPS baseline of 78.0p;

desk.headline: Underlying EPS up 22% to 36.5p on record £6.7bn investment; 2026/27 EPS growth guidance raised to 15–16%
results: Underlying EPS rose 22% to 36.5p and underlying operating profit 13% to £2.59bn, helped by the new UK transmission price control (RIIO-T3), US rate-base growth and one-off investment gains.
Statutory profit before tax more than doubled to £1.73bn and statutory EPS was 26.9p, boosted by timing effects and exceptional gains.
Capital investment hit a record £6.7bn, up a third, led by UK Electricity Transmission (up 71% at constant currency).
Interim dividend of 16.97p, up 4%; net debt rose to £48.6bn, partly to fund the $1.75bn Joulent investment.

guidance.summary: Underlying EPS for 2026/27 is now expected to grow 15–16% from the 78.0p base, up from the original 13–15% range, with about £13.5bn of capital investment. The five-year plan (at least £70bn of investment, 8–10% a year EPS growth) is unchanged.

points: The CFO said the original 13–15% EPS range was lifted on operating progress and one-off gains in the National Grid Partners portfolio.
CEO Zoë Yujnovich highlighted faster capital delivery, with over 80% of the supply chain for the £70bn plan already secured.
The Joulent stake backs the 2.7 GW Kilby power project for a Microsoft data centre in Texas; more projects only if they clear return hurdles.
Management acknowledged bill pressure for customers and pointed to interconnector payments and a one-year New York gas rate freeze.
Net debt is expected to rise about another £4bn in the second half; US rate cases should lift returns gradually, not sharply.
call.source: Results call transcript: The Motley Fool, 5 Nov 2026

watch: Ofgem's response to the ED3 distribution business plan due at the end of November.
The Massachusetts gas rate decision expected within about a month.
Growth in net debt and gearing as investment ramps up toward £13.5bn this year.
